# PR #3366: Patch: cards that move like cards: a flight from hand to tile, a deck that riffles when shuffled, an opening deal, a hand that springs, and a drag that tilts with its speed

Closes #3347

Cards in the web client now move like cards: a hand play flies from where the drag let go, decks riffle when shuffled, the opening hand is dealt a card at a time, the fan springs, and the drag ghost tilts and springs home on a miss. Everything is client-side and driven by public events and the player's own input (CLAUDE.md rule 7). `crates/`, `spec/`, the wire files and the engine's events are untouched, and no patch fragment was added.

## What changed

- **Hand to tile.** The effects layer already flew a stand-in from hand to zone. It now starts at the pointer's release point and turns toward its tile (`--fx-rot`). It still lands inside the play row's time, and opponent plays still fly as backs from `hand-opponent`. While it flies, the old landing ghost hides. At full motion the ghost also now stays at the release point instead of jumping to the zone centre.
- **Riffle.** `riffleEntries` marks the last `shuffledIn` or `traded` of an action, so there is one riffle per action. That entry is lengthened by `RIFFLE_MS`, scaled by Speed, and the leaves are drawn in the Deck pile. A mulligan's returned cards now fly from their hand. The audio director plays one `riffle` sound per action, including on the reduced-motion flush path.
- **Opening deal.** A game whose first view is in the mulligan phase gets a riffle sound, then one `deal` sound and one card flight per card, `DEAL_STAGGER_MS` apart, the opponent's as backs. It reads only hand counts. Reduced motion has no deal. Effects off keeps the sounds and drops the flights. A tap ends it.
- **Hand spring.** `useHandSpring` springs slots on `translate` when the fan reflows, using `--ease-overshoot` at full motion. Hovering a card parts its neighbours.
- **Drag.** The ghost tilts with pointer speed up to `DRAG_TILT_MAX_DEG` and settles flat after `DRAG_TILT_SETTLE_MS`. The tile under it gets `data-drag-over`. A card let go over nothing springs back to its slot.
- **Sounds and haptic.** Six new sounds: `pickUp`, `dragOver`, `drop`, `returnToHand`, `deal`, `riffle`. A pick-up buzz is added. A shared haptics instance gives the pick-up buzz and the existing drop buzz one gap clock.
- **Settings.** `cardMotionLevel` gives `still` (reduced motion), `calm` (effects off) or `full`, written as `data-card-motion`.

## How it was tested

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main`: 433 files, 8284 tests passed, 74 skipped. This run included the audio and fx suites, the style ratchets and the wording tests. An earlier broader run timed out on the wording tests under CPU load; they passed in this run.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint` on all 40 changed and new TypeScript files, and `pnpm --dir e2e run typecheck:component` are clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` (1799 rulings, ok), `patches check` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. `classify` reports `App`, and there is no diff under `apps/web/src/wire`.
- **Not run:** Cypress. `e2e/cypress/component/card-motion.cy.tsx` (flight, riffle, deal and tilted drag at 1280×720 and 390×844) is checked by typecheck and eslint only. I also did not run e2e `16` and `25`.

New tests: `animations.riffle.test.ts`, `opening.test.ts`, `Game.opening.test.tsx`, `handSpring.test.tsx`, `drag/tilt.test.ts`, and additions to the drag-layer, haptics, audio-director, `sfx`, Hand, stage, dom and cues tests. I also changed two existing assertions and added the two new fx constants to the S2 constants table. `animations.test.ts` now expects the riffle's added time. `motion.test.ts` has `ANIM_SCALED["game/board.css"]` 12→13. The `Board.test.tsx` snapshot adds only the `pile-riffle` span on both Deck piles.

## Decisions the plan or issue did not settle

- **A tap during the deal ends it but is not swallowed.** The plan said to stop propagation. That would eat the first press of the mulligan's Keep, which the e2e specs click straight away. Swallowing instead would mean the first tap only skips the deal.
- **Landing ghost position.** At full motion the landing ghost stays at the release point, so the stand-in's flight starts from where the ghost already is. Otherwise it jumped to the zone centre first. Under reduced motion or effects off it goes to the tile as before.
- **Return sound scope.** `returnToHand` and `pickUp` fire only for a hand-card play drag, not an attack arrow.
- **Return and drop rules.** The return fires on any non-consumed release, including a refused drop on a locked zone. A drop sound fires when a legal drop lands, meaning an action sent or a build advanced, not only when an action is sent. A play lifted again from its zone with a pending build counts as consumed, so no spring home.
- **Hand spring measurement.** It measures `offsetLeft`, which ignores transforms, instead of `getBoundingClientRect`, so a hover or a spring in flight is not read as a move.
- **Effects off.** The riffle takes 0 ms in the queue at intensity off, so the entry is not held for leaves nobody sees. The sound stays.
- **Speed.** The drag's spring home is scaled by Speed.
- **Not built.** `--deal-stagger` is not written, because nothing reads it. The hand reorder gap has no client feature to attach to.
- **File naming.** `handSpring.test.tsx` is `.tsx`, not `.ts`, because it renders JSX. The release-point test and the stage tests are in `fx/stage.test.tsx`, which has the director harness. `--fx-rot` tests are in `fx/dom.test.ts`.

## Worth a second look

- `DragLayer.tsx`: the `stopDragging(consumed)` change and the tilt-timer cleanup.
- The `Game.tsx` opening effect, whose timers belong to an effect keyed on `opening` so StrictMode's double run cannot strand `data-dealing` (a test covers it).
- `[data-drag-over]` is a hook for #3342, which is unmerged, so it may want to restyle it.
- A reconnect during the mulligan replays the deal, because the board cannot tell it from a first load.
- `fitBudget` can shorten an entry under a long riffle, in which case the riffle simply ends early.

## Player note

Cards now fly from your hand to their tile, decks riffle when shuffled, your opening hand is dealt one card at a time, your hand fans with a little spring, and a dragged card tilts as you move it and springs back if you let go over nothing, each with a soft sound, all of it following your Speed, Reduce motion and effects settings.

# #3347: Patch: cards that move like cards: a flight from hand to tile, a deck that riffles when shuffled, an opening deal, a hand that springs, and a drag that tilts with its speed
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

## What it does

Part of #3330. The owner asked that cards moving around feel like real cards: "there should be shuffles", and so on.

### Today

- **Dropping a card.** `game/drag/landing.ts` hides it from the fan, `jk-card-played` lifts and fades it at the hand, then `jk-summon-scale` and a silhouette drop at the zone. There is **no continuous flight** from hand to tile.
- **No shuffle and no deal.** Nothing animates a deck shuffle or the opening deal. `shuffledIn` (one card into a library) and `traded` pulse the library pile (`jk-shuffle-in`). There is no deck-shuffle event, and the opening deal has no motion.
- **The hand fan** reflows with plain transitions. The drag ghost (`DragLayer.tsx`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX` 8) follows the pointer flat.
- **Card-back flights** cover draw, bounce and discard (`fx/cues.ts` `ghost` cues).

### What it should be

All of this is client-side presentation, keyed on public events and the player's own input (CLAUDE.md rule 7). The engine needs no new event.

1. **Hand to tile.** A card played from hand flies on an arc from where it left the hand (or where the drag let go) to its tile, turning to face it and growing to its board size, then lands with the summon row. Its time comes out of the existing play row's time, and the `--anim-squeeze` scaling holds. The opponent's plays fly from their hand's edge, face down until the view shows them.
2. **The riffle.** The library riffles when it is shuffled:
   - at the game's start, before the deal;
   - after a `shuffledIn` or `traded` (one riffle per action, however many cards went in);
   - on a mulligan, the returned cards fly into the deck and it riffles.

   The riffle is the pile's top cards splitting and interleaving, with a riffle sound (`audio/sfx.ts`).
3. **The opening deal.** The opening hand is dealt one card at a time from the deck to the hand, with a flick sound each, `DEAL_STAGGER_MS` apart. The opponent's hand is dealt face down. A tap skips it.
4. **A hand that springs.** The fan reflows on a spring when a card leaves or arrives, instead of a linear transition: a slight overshoot with `--ease-overshoot`. Hovering lifts and spreads the neighbours. Dragging a card over the hand to reorder it (where the client already allows it) parts the cards around the gap.
5. **A drag with weight.** The drag ghost tilts in the direction it moves, by its speed, up to `DRAG_TILT_MAX_DEG`, and settles flat when still. Over a legal tile, the tile lifts to meet it (#3342's tile feedback). Released over nothing, it springs back to its place in the hand.
6. **Sounds and buzzes.** Pick-up, drag-over-tile, drop, return-to-hand, draw, deal and riffle each have a soft sound of their own, on the sfx bus at a low level. On a phone, pick-up and drop give a light haptic (`haptics/`, with the Vibration setting and `HAPTIC_MIN_GAP_MS`).
7. **Settings.** Speed scales it all (R201), reduced motion snaps each move to its end with no flight, and fx intensity off keeps the sounds but drops the flourishes.

## Acceptance

- Tests (`animations.test.ts`, drag tests and new ones):
  - a hand play flies within its row's time;
  - the riffle plays once per action at the game's start, after `shuffledIn` or `traded`, and on a mulligan;
  - the deal is staggered and skippable;
  - the opponent's cards stay face down until the view shows them.
- The drag tilt follows speed up to its cap and settles. A released drag returns to its place.
- Each sound and haptic fires once per event, under its settings.
- A component spec captures a flight, a riffle, the deal and a tilted drag at desktop size and at 390x844. e2e `16` (drag to play) and `25` (overflow animations) pass.
- `src/motion.test.ts` and `fx/css.test.ts` pass, and every number is a named constant.
- The web tests, `typecheck` and `eslint` pass, and the pull request carries a `## Player note`.
